gates.text: All PRD acceptance criteria have test cases
Edge cases and error conditions identified
No AC names an aspirational verification mechanism (#2424 gate — all named mechanisms already in use in this repo; see `.claude/metadata/ac-feasibility-prompts.json`)

_meta.purpose: The single declaration of the test-plan approval gate set. Both rendered surfaces — the `## Approval Checklist` in Templates/artifacts/test-plan-template.md and the `## Review Checklist` in the approval issue written by /create-prd Phase 6.6 — are rendered from the `text` values here, in this order. Before this file existed the two surfaces were independently worded restatements that had already diverged: six items against five.
_meta.textIsCanonical: `text` is the rendered string, not a label. Editing it changes both surfaces, and tests/metadata/test-plan-approval-gates.test.js fails if either surface stops matching. Gate `no-aspirational-mechanism` additionally has its wording pinned by tests/commands/test-plan-template-ac-feasibility-line.test.js (#2425), whose regex requires the phrase 'aspirational verification mechanism', the '#2424' reference and the ac-feasibility-prompts.json path to survive together.
_meta.autoCheckable: Whether the gate can be resolved by the deterministic rollup over review findings (#2711) rather than needing human confirmation (#2712). The first five gates map onto objective criteria that each carry an autoCheckMethod, so a finding set determines them. `no-aspirational-mechanism` is deliberately false: its backing criterion can grep for a mechanism's existing usage, but deciding whether an AC *names a verification mechanism at all* is a reading of prose, and a gate that claims to be computed while resting on that judgment would report false confidence. False here means 'always needs a human', not 'not yet implemented'.
_meta.criteriaCoverage: Every gate names at least one backing criterion — the defect this file closes was gate `no-aspirational-mechanism` shipping with none, leaving it checked on judgment or skipped silently. The converse does not hold and is not asserted: `test-framework-specified`, `test-levels-defined` and `framework-consistent` back no gate, because they describe how the plan declares its framework rather than any approval gate. A criterion without a gate is still evaluated during review; a gate without a criterion had no evaluator at all.
